extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the required form, content, arrangement, and electronic submission rules for U.S. patent applications (specification, drawings, sequence listings, compact discs, translations, and related papers). Covers examiner objection practices and procedural consequences for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact disc submission in duplicate
rubrics_metrics.description: Any compact disc must be submitted in duplicate unless it contains only the 'Sequence Listing' in computer readable form required by § 1.821(e). The compact disc and duplicate copy must be labeled 'Copy 1' and 'Copy 2,' respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transmittal letter must state that the two compact discs are identical; if not identical, the Office will use the disc labeled 'Copy 1' for processing. Any amendment to information on a compact disc must be by replacement disc complying with these rules and accompanied by a statement that the replacement contains no new matter. Replacement discs must be labeled 'COPY 1 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' and 'COPY 2 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' with creation dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact disc file identification and contents disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must contain an incorporation-by-reference of the material on the compact disc in a separate paragraph (§ 1.77(b)(5)), identifying each compact disc by the names of the files contained, their date of creation and their sizes in bytes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require the applicant to amend the paper portion to include any part previously submitted on compact disc. Compact discs submitted to the Office will not be returned to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact disc labeling information
rubrics_metrics.description: A compact disc must be labeled with the following information: (i) name of each inventor (if known); (ii) title of the invention; (iii) docket number or application number if known; (iv) creation date of the compact disc; (v) if multiple discs, indicate order (e.g., '1 of X'); (vi) indicate whether 'Copy 1' or 'Copy 2'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraph (b)(4) for duplicate labeling rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreadable electronic files treated as not submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: If a file is unreadable on both copies of the disc, the unreadable file will be treated as not having been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A file is unreadable if it is of a format that does not comply with requirements, is corrupted by a computer virus, or is written onto a defective compact disc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listings and program listings excluded from application size fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Any sequence listing in an electronic medium in compliance with §§ 1.52(e) and 1.821(c) or (e), and any computer program listing filed in an electronic medium in compliance with §§ 1.52(e) and 1.96, will be excluded when determining the application size fee required by § 1.16(s) or § 1.492(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the listing is submitted in ASCII text as part of an associated file via the Office electronic filing system it will be excluded for fee determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper-size equivalent for electronic media (non-EFS submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications where specification and drawings (excluding compliant sequence listings and program listings) are submitted in whole or in part on an electronic medium other than the Office electronic filing system, each three kilobytes of content submitted on an electronic medium shall be counted as a sheet of paper for application size fee purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This counting applies only to electronic media submitted outside the Office electronic filing system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper-size equivalent for EFS-Web submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper size equivalent of specification and drawings of an application submitted via the Office electronic filing system will be considered to be seventy-five percent of the number of sheets of paper present when rendered by the Office electronic filing system for purposes of determining the application size fee required by § 1.16(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings and computer program listings submitted via EFS-Web in ASCII text are excluded from the size determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical and mathematical formulae and tables allowed (but not drawings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification, including the claims, may contain chemical and mathematical formulae, but shall not contain drawings or flow diagrams. The description portion may contain tables, but the same tables should not be included in both the drawings and description portion of the specification. Claims may contain tables if necessary to conform to 35 U.S.C. 112 or otherwise desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphical illustrations/flowcharts belong in drawings (see 37 CFR 1.81) and examiners should object to descriptive illustrations in the specification and request drawings when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic tables must preserve spatial relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables submitted in electronic form (§§ 1.96(c) and 1.821(c)) must maintain the spatial relationships (e.g., alignment of columns and rows) of the table elements when displayed so as to visually preserve the relational information they convey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chemical and mathematical formulae must be encoded to maintain the proper positioning of their characters when displayed to preserve intended meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font and sizing requirements for formulae/tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Typewritten characters used in formulae and tables must be chosen from a block (nonscript) type font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, or Courier) with capital letters which should be at least 0.422 cm (0.166 inch) high (preferably font size 12), but may be no smaller than 0.21 cm (0.08 inch) high (font size 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulae and tables may be placed in landscape orientation if they cannot be presented satisfactorily in portrait orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page numbering and line spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: The pages of the specification, including claims and abstract, must be numbered consecutively starting with 1, the numbers being centrally located above or preferably below the text. The lines of the specification and any amendments must be 1 1/2 or double spaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text must be written in a nonscript type font (preferably font size 12) with capital letters at least 0.3175 cm (0.125 inch) high but no smaller than 0.21 cm (0.08 inch) (font size 6). The text may not be written solely in capital letters and only a single column of text is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate sheets for specification elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must commence on a separate sheet. Each sheet including part of the specification may not include other parts of the application or other information. The claim(s), abstract and sequence listing (if any) should not be included on a sheet including any other part of the application. The claim(s) must commence on a separate sheet or electronic page and any sheet including a claim or portion of a claim may not contain any other parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract must commence on a separate sheet and any sheet including an abstract or portion thereof may not contain any other parts of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable paper sizes and uniformity
rubrics_metrics.description: All application papers that are submitted on paper or by facsimile which are to become part of the permanent USPTO record must be on sheets of paper which are the same size and are either 21.0 cm by 29.7 cm (DIN A4) or 21.6 cm by 27.9 cm (8 1/2 by 11 inches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment should not have two different sizes of paper; however, specification and drawings may be different sizes (e.g., drawings can be larger).

rubrics_metrics.name: Page margins and no holes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each sheet, other than the drawings, must include a top margin of at least 2.0 cm (3/4 inch), a left side margin of at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), a right side margin of at least 2.0 cm (3/4 inch), and a bottom margin of at least 2.0 cm (3/4 inch). No holes should be made in the sheets as submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper quality, ink, and legibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers which are to become part of the permanent records must be legibly written either by a typewriter or mechanical printer in permanent dark ink or its equivalent in portrait orientation on flexible, strong, smooth, nonshiny, durable, and white paper. Typed, mimeographed, xeroprinted, multigraphed or nonsmearing carbon copy forms of reproduction are acceptable. 'Easily Erasable' coated paper may not provide a 'permanent' copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legibility includes suitability for photocopying and scanning so that reprints can be made and paper can be electronically reproduced by digital imaging and optical character recognition; high contrast (black on white) is required. Gray lines/backgrounds reduce reproduction quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and correction for noncompliant application papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is filed with papers that do not comply with 37 CFR 1.52, the Office will mail a 'Notice to File the Corrected Application Papers' identifying the deficiency and setting a time period within which the applicant must correct the deficiencies to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit compliant papers does not affect the grant of a filing date; original noncompliant papers will be retained in the application file as the original disclosure. The USPTO will not return papers simply because they do not comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legible substitute specification required
rubrics_metrics.description: If the specification or amendments are not presented plainly and legibly as required, a legible substitute specification in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b) and 1.125 is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: identify which part is illegible (all or certain pages). Do not use the form paragraph for reissue applications or reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-signing alterations and oath/declaration applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Interlineations and other alterations of the application papers may be made after signing of the inventor's oath or declaration (37 CFR 1.52(c) no longer prohibits this).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If alterations are made after signing, statements in the inventor's oath or declaration pursuant to 37 CFR 1.63 must remain applicable to the application papers; otherwise a new inventor's oath or declaration may be required. See MPEP § 602.08(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies of application-as-filed may be illegible if original noncompliant
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application-as-filed does not meet sheet size/margin and quality requirements, certified copies of such application may be illegible and/or ineffective as priority documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the USPTO provides a certified copy it will make a copy from the records in the IFW or microfilm database; exception processing (scaling/reduction/enhancement) may be required and certified copies of the application-as-filed may not be legible. Substitute papers filed later do not change the content of the application-as-filed for certified copy purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use metric (S.I.) units recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should use the metric (S.I.) units followed by the equivalent English units when describing dimensions in specifications to minimize future conversions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance explains S.I. origins and rationale for recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English filing — translation and accuracy statement required (nonprovisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonprovisional application is filed in a language other than English, an English language translation of the non-English application, a statement that the translation is accurate, and the processing fee set forth in § 1.17(i) are required. If these items are not filed with the application, applicant will be notified and given time to file them to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For provisional applications filed in a non-English language, an English translation is not required at filing but will be required later if benefit is claimed in a later-filed nonprovisional application (see § 1.78(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation requirements and use for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A subsequently filed English translation must be a literal translation, accompanied by a statement that the translation is accurate, and by a signed request from applicant or agent asking that the English translation be used as the copy for examination purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the translation does not conform to idiomatic English and U.S. practice, it should be accompanied by a preliminary amendment making necessary changes without introducing new matter. If timely translations/statement are not filed, the nonprovisional application will be regarded as abandoned. If published, the translation is the document that is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended practices for filing non-English papers
rubrics_metrics.description: It is strongly recommended that the original non-English application papers be filed via EFS-Web or be accompanied by a cover letter and a self-addressed return postcard containing identifying data in English (applicant name(s); title of invention; number of pages; whether an oath/declaration filed; amount and manner of paying fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is to permit prompt association of a subsequently filed English translation with the initial papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid routine use of emergency filing practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a non-English application with a later translation or filing by reference to a previously filed application are practices intended for emergency situations to prevent loss of rights and should not be routinely used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons include danger of incorrect literal translations and administrative burdens on the Office. See also MPEP § 601.01(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations/flowcharts in descriptive portion are improper
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical illustrations, diagrammatic views, flowcharts, and diagrams in the descriptive portion of the specification do not come within 37 CFR 1.58(a) and examiners should object to such descriptive illustrations and request drawings in accordance with 37 CFR 1.81.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written description must not contain drawings or flow diagrams. Claims may incorporate by reference to a specific figure or table where practical definition in words is not possible. The description should not duplicate tables that appear in drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlinks and browser-executable code not permitted for incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference by hyperlink or other browser-executable code is not permitted (37 CFR 1.57(e)). Examiners must review applications and object to embedded hyperlinks or other browser-executable code in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are required to delete embedded hyperlinks and limit website references to the top-level domain name without any prefix such as 'http://'. Examples of hyperlinks are URLs placed between '< >' or 'http://...'. Nucleotide/amino acid sequence data placed between '< >' are not considered hyperlinks and should not be objected to. If the hyperlink/code itself (not the site contents) is part of the invention and is necessary to meet 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and applicant does not intend active links, examiners should not object; the Office will disable hyperlinks when loading to the USPTO web database. Use form paragraph 7.29.04 for objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement/order of application elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of the application, if applicable, should appear in the following order: (1) utility application transmittal form; (2) fee transmittal form; (3) application data sheet (§ 1.76); (4) specification; (5) drawings; (6) inventor's oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the preferred order per 37 CFR 1.77(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification section order and headings
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should include the following sections in order (if applicable): title of the invention; cross-reference to related applications; statement regarding federally sponsored research; names of parties to a joint research agreement; reference to Sequence Listing/table/computer program appendix on compact disc and incorporation-by-reference; statement regarding prior disclosures; background of the invention; brief summary; brief description of views of drawings; detailed description; claim(s); abstract; Sequence Listing (if on paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text of these sections should be preceded by a section heading in uppercase without underlining or bold type. If no text follows, the phrase 'Not Applicable' should follow the heading. Provisional applications are recommended to follow the same format though claims are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) controls certain information (post-2012 filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, if there is a discrepancy between information in an application data sheet and elsewhere in the application, the application data sheet will control except for naming of inventors. The most recent compliant ADS will govern with respect to foreign priority or domestic benefit claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For filings before September 16, 2012, different pre-AIA rules about ADS control apply; naming inventors and citizenship remain governed by specific CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title content and length requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention should be placed at the top of the first page of the specification unless provided in an application data sheet. The title should be brief but technically accurate and descriptive, preferably from two to seven words, and may not contain more than 500 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.72(a) and MPEP § 606 for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background of the invention should include field and related art
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should set forth the Background of the Invention in two parts: (1) Field of the Invention — a statement of the field of art (may be titled 'Technical Field'); and (2) Description of the Related Art — a description of related art known to the applicant including references to specific related art and problems solved by the invention (may be titled 'Background Art').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include information disclosed under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 where applicable.
